item.title: Solved: Total Memory Usage in a Python Process
item.description:
Is it possible to gauge the total memory utilized by a Python program? While many discussions surround the memory consumption of individual objects, it becomes crucial to ascertain the overall memory usage for the process. This measurement is essential for deciding when to purge cached data effectively. Here, we will delve into the solutions available for different operating environments.

Top 6 Methods to Check Total Memory Usage in Python

Method 1: Using getrusage() on Unix Systems

For Unix-like systems, such as Linux and Mac OS X, the getrusage() function can be harnessed from the resource module in Python. This function returns memory usage statistics, including peak memory usage for the calling process accessible via the ru_maxrss attribute.

item.title: Top 11 Methods to Determine the Size of an Object in Python
item.description:
Top 11 Methods to Determine the Size of an Object in Python

Determining the size of an object in Python can sometimes feel like a puzzling task, especially when your objects contain additional data structures or other complex data types. This post aims to walk you through various methods to calculate the memory size occupied by objects in Python, ranging from built-in functions to third-party packages and custom solutions.

Method 1: Using sys.getsizeof

One of the most straightforward methods to get the size of an object is with the built-in sys.getsizeof(obj) function. Note, however, that this function only returns the memory size of the object passed and does not account for the memory consumed by nested objects.
